### Iteration 140 — 2026-09-20 ~18:10–19:00 UTC (claude-opus, work): CR-85.2 — the vendor card, which is the first source the CR names

- **Why this and not something else.** The 172003Z gate left CR-85.2 `in-progress` for "the vendor card, OpenRouter, Epoch and
  remaining exact-source/category work". Of those, iteration 125 had already audited OpenRouter (already pinned) and Epoch
  (publishes V4 Flash, not an exact V4.1 identity) and had closed them as refusals. Its own first *remaining* item was the one
  nobody had done: "capture and review the official release page/model-card material as self-reported evidence **if the project
  wants those claims displayed**." CR-85.2's text is that permission, in Florian's own words — "DeepSeek's release notes/model
  card (self-reported, mark as vendor-reported) … ingest each with provenance" — and CR-98 had shipped the mechanism for exactly
  this shape of row nine hours earlier. So the gap was a document nobody had captured, not a decision nobody could make.
- **The trap, found before it shipped.** The card prints its results twice: once in "Comparison with frontier models (Max
  reasoning effort)", whose columns are models, and once in "Performance across agent scaffolds", whose columns are harnesses
  and which repeats two of the same row labels. The first parser split the file on the first heading and kept reading, so
  column 7 of the scaffold table — DSH Standard — came back as the model's own DeepSWE (70.5) and Terminal-Bench 2.1 (85.8)
  instead of 74.2 and 90.6. The fix is that the parser is bounded to one contiguous pipe table, and
  `test/deepseek-v41-flash-claims.test.mjs` re-derives all 19 values from the capture rather than trusting the shipped file.
  The live verifier checks the same thing from the other side: no other scaffold's number is served for either board.
- **What the refusals cost, and why they are worth it.** Nine claims from the same document are recorded as refused with their
  reasons: the base-model table (21 values — the catalog has no base checkpoint), the per-scaffold breakdown (16 values), the
  four other labs' columns, DeepSeek's own DS-V4-Pro and DS-V4-Flash columns, and the footnoted HLE text-only 39.1. The last
  two are the interesting ones. The sibling columns are DeepSeek's own models, so the "only the publishing lab's own models"
  rule does *not* exclude them — what excludes them is that the card prints no checkpoint while the catalog carries
  `deepseek-v4-pro::max` / `deepseek-v4-pro-0813::max` and `deepseek-v4-flash::max` / `deepseek-v4-flash-0731::max`. Guessing
  would have added roughly 30 more rows; the identity is genuinely ambiguous, so nothing joined.
- **The critic round was widened, not narrowed.** The first slice passed on findings but listed four `missing_evidence` items,
  and `verifyScoreEvidence` requires that list to be empty. Rather than instruct the critic to stop reporting them, the packet
  was rebuilt to contain what it had asked for: the full Evaluation Results section including the base table, every DeepSeek
  V4-family id in the catalog, and all 19 identities and values in both slices. Both slices then returned
  `errors_found: 0`, `findings: []`, `missing_evidence: []` — `z-ai/glm-5.3-flash`, producer `anthropic/claude-opus-5`,
  deliberately not a DeepSeek model, since DeepSeek is the vendor under review.
- **Two shipped tests were generalised rather than given a third hardcoded source.** `test/self-reported-vendor.test.mjs` had a
  StepFun-specific branch for the locator checks. It now requires any release-document row to name the printed row it was read
  from *and* that the named row contains the registry entry's own name — a stricter rule than the URL special case it replaced,
  and one that a fourth vendor document will satisfy without another edit. `test/benchmark-view.test.mjs`'s payload ceiling went
  650 KB → 675 KB for 19 axes of metadata, with the reason recorded in the comment chain like every raise before it.
- **Gates for `4cf8d10`:** `node scripts/build-dataset.mjs`, `npm test` 971 (970 pass, 1 skipped), `npx tsc --noEmit -p .`,
  `npm run build`, `git diff --check`. Data diff strictly additive: +19 observations, 0 removed, 0 unrelated joins.
- **Live at `4cf8d100da080368ee38470467006d0e20b29a55` on both hosts: 109/109 and 109/109**
  (`/opt/benchmarkheaven/state/ux-evidence/iter140-cr85-2-deepseek/{canonical,legacy}/verification.json`). The verifier
  re-derives every expected value from the committed capture instead of reading our own dataset back, and pins the honesty
  properties: all 19 rows `self_reported` with the replacement rule, every card board carrying exactly one row, the HLE
  text-only figure absent, the Composite unchanged at 77.418 on 1 of 7 inputs with 0 attached. The page says it in its own
  words: *"19 of 40 values are DeepSeek's own claims (†), not independent measurements; a matching independent result
  replaces a claim as soon as one exists."*
- **A pre-existing data-loss bug found on the way, and fixed.** `scripts/collect-self-reported-scores.mjs` rewrites
  `self-reported-candidates.json` wholesale from the locked 2026-09-16 scout extraction. It is not in the daily pipeline, but a
  hand run **did** delete CR-98's 40 Step-5 rows and these 19 — measured, not assumed: a run against the shipped file took it
  from 97 observations to 38. Both populations had been added directly, as the CR-98 commit did, and the scout extraction
  cannot produce either. Fixed in the follow-up commit: `data/raw/benchmarks/self-reported/carried-documents.json` lists the
  hand-ingested release documents by URL, `carryReviewedDocuments` in `lib/self-reported-vendor.mjs` carries their
  observations, collections and refusals through a rebuild, and the collector re-checks each carried row against its own
  retained capture before it survives. It fails closed both ways: a listed document that contributes nothing throws (its rows
  were already lost), and a carried id that the scout also produces throws. **Proof: a rebuild now leaves the file
  byte-identical** (md5 `c823ca0a53ce98ce0b2a156987b5d9fa` before and after, 97 observations, 59 carried). A third test pins
  the invariant that keeps this from recurring — every source URL in the candidates file is either in the scout's own locked
  capture manifest or on the carry list, and the carry list never names a document the scout already owns.
- **The question a reviewer should ask, asked and answered: can a lab's own numbers move its Benchmaxxing signal?** Neither
  `measuredAxisMaps` nor `evidencedAxisMaps` filters on `basis`, so the 19 new axes (and CR-98's 40 before them) do reach the
  Benchmaxxing view — the radar profile for this model goes from 310 to 329 axes. They cannot move anything, and the reason is
  structural rather than lucky: `computePairStats` is built from the **measured** maps, and a board whose only row is a vendor
  claim has a measured cohort of **0**, so it forms no pair and enters no prediction. Measured both ways: every one of the 19
  card axes has cohort size 0, and `scoreBenchmaxxing` returns **7.6026927493156595 before and after**, identical to the digit.
  `test/deepseek-v41-flash-claims.test.mjs` now pins both, so a later change that starts feeding claims into the pair
  statistics fails there rather than quietly moving a tag.
- **The CR's two remaining sources for this model, checked rather than assumed.** `designarena` is `{}` for
  `deepseek-v4.1-flash::max` and the Lumina ledger does not mention the model at all (0 occurrences). So DesignArena is empty

- **Checked that tomorrow's 05:17 run will not trip over the new entries.** Neither the 19 DeepSeek nor the 40 Step-5

## Iteration 143 (continued) — 2026-09-21 02:05 → 02:30 UTC (claude-opus, work): LiveBench unfrozen, and why four more sources cannot pass

- **LiveBench fixed** (commit `6da24fa`). `livebench.ai` rebuilt on 2026-09-17; the content-hashed bundle it pinned became a 404 and
  the board retained its old snapshot for four days. The bundle is now **discovered from the page's own script tag** (`page_url` +
  `follow_module_script`, the route ApprenticeBench already used) instead of pinned by filename. The discovery regex only knew the
  Vite form; it now also knows the CRA `static/js/main.<hash>.js` form, still requires exactly one match, and resolves the src
  against the page URL. Both parser guard literals are present in the new bundle exactly once. No value, id or join moved — only the
  `frontend_source` provenance of all 57 observations.
- **A systemic defect, found while fixing it.** `ops/daily/refresh-benchmarks.mjs` requires an evidence `excerpt` to appear
  **verbatim** in any source over 60 kB, otherwise the source fails with *"methodology passage changed or unavailable in a large
  primary page"*. An excerpt written as a *description* can therefore never pass — and LiveBench's bundle excerpt was one.
- **The four MathArena identities have the same shape and are deliberately not fixed here.** Their
  `competition_tables/arxiv--june|august` evidence carries a described excerpt ("Leaderboard columns: Rank | Model Name | …; 22 model
  rows; 48 problem columns") on pages of **1.3 MB and 563 kB**; re-fetched on 2026-09-21, the phrase "Leaderboard columns" does not
  occur on either page at all. Their real methodology sources, `/competitions` and `/arxivmath`, **do** carry verbatim excerpts —
  all four re-checked against the live page today and present. The fix is to stop treating a data capture as a protocol reference:
  the registry's own convention for that is `source_sha256` on the evidence entry (25 AA / OpenRouter / Real-SWE entries use it, and
  `references` is filtered by `!s.source_sha256`). **Left for the next iteration on purpose** — it changes the protocol-review gate
  for four identities and cannot be exercised offline, so it should land behind a `gated-run.sh --dry-run`. `aa-benchmark-fields`
  (failing since **2026-09-11**, receipt: "zuletzt gut: nie") is very likely the same defect and is the one to check first.
  `frontierswe::2` is a different problem: `https://epoch.ai/data-download?search=frontierswe` now 404s and its Epoch relay needs a
  new URL.
- **Live at `6da24fa` on both hosts:** LiveBench still publishes the same measured values from the matrix API
  (`gpt-5.6-sol::max` 81.05, `gemini-3.5-flash::high` 74.64, both basis 0), and `bin/verify-cr-30-mcp-atlas.mjs` is **30/30 per host**
  again at this revision (`/opt/benchmarkheaven/state/ux-evidence/iter143-mcp-atlas/{canonical,legacy}-6da24fa/`).
- Gates: `build-dataset` rc 0, `npm test` **991 tests, 990 pass, 0 fail, 1 skip**, `npx tsc --noEmit -p .` clean, `npm run build`
  35/35 pages, `git diff --check` clean.

  - `aaFieldActivity(rootField, changed, old)` counts, per affected AA field, the model rows whose value was added (on rows that had none before), changed, or newly nulled. Only added-or-changed **values** are affirmative; removals count separately (`removed`) and never imply liveness — a board being wound down also edits its field.
  - `aaActivitySource(receipt, activity)` puts that summary in the protocol packet, riding the same capture receipt hash, its locator plainly stating it is a generated summary, not maintainer text.
  - One criteria sentence joins the lifecycle criterion: when the packet carries this run's own added/changed-value count, a nonzero count is affirmative evidence for `status: "active"` **for this board only**; it settles nothing about methodology/task set/harness/version and can never establish `"retained"`. Public boards are untouched — they never carry the summary, and the sentence is conditional on its presence. `PROTOCOL_REVIEW_CRITERIA.length` stays 2.
  - `protocol()` cache key now includes the field so two fields mapping to one entry get one review each, and a plain public-arm call never reads a field-tagged one.
